name: Carborundum Universal Limited

moat_sources.name: pricing_power
moat_sources.evidence_note: Domestic abrasives leadership supports some price realization, but FY25 saw a reported ~350bps gross-margin contraction and consolidated EBITDA margin fell to ~15-16% (vs a standalone 21.5% in FY26) -- limited ability to fully pass through raw-material/forex swings in a price-competitive industrial-consumables market.

moat_sources.name: switching_costs
moat_sources.evidence_note: Abrasives/ceramics are qualified into industrial customers' process specs (auto, bearings, general engineering), creating some re-qualification friction, but credible alternative suppliers (domestic + Chinese imports, 3M, Saint-Gobain/Norton) exist, limiting true lock-in.

moat_sources.name: network_effects
moat_sources.evidence_note: Not applicable / absent -- industrial abrasives, ceramics, refractories and electrominerals manufacturing has no network-effect dynamic; it is a materials and component business, not a platform.

moat_sources.name: cost_advantage
moat_sources.evidence_note: Backward integration into electrominerals (captive fused alumina / silicon carbide production, the segment that grew fastest in FY25 at +11.1%) gives a real raw-material cost and security advantage vs abrasive-only competitors; Murugappa Group manufacturing scale reinforces sourcing leverage and overhead absorption as domestic volumes recover.

moat_sources.name: intangible_assets
moat_sources.evidence_note: 70+ year CUMI brand carries real trust in Indian industrial-consumables trade channels, and technical-ceramics/engineered-refractories know-how is sold into EV, semiconductor and aerospace-adjacent applications, but this is a modest IP moat relative to global majors (3M, Saint-Gobain) and not independently verified via patent data in this pass.

moat_sources.name: efficient_scale
moat_sources.evidence_note: One of India's largest abrasives producers, widely cited at >30% domestic market share, with capital-intensive plants that raise entry barriers for new domestic players; the same scale ambition drove overseas expansion (Russia, Germany, South Africa) that has recently required write-downs and unit closures -- scale is real domestically, execution abroad has been mixed.

industry_context.phase_evidence: Global/domestic industrial abrasives-ceramics-refractories-electrominerals market is mature and tracks industrial production, auto and general capex cycles rather than a structural adoption curve. Domestic abrasives leadership (~30%+ share, widely cited) is entrenched but not visibly gaining: consolidated revenue grew only ~2.9% CAGR FY23-FY26 (4731 -> 5149 Cr) despite standalone (largely domestic) growth of 8.6% in FY26, dragged down by overseas units. Genuine higher-growth pockets exist in technical ceramics for EV/semiconductor/aerospace-adjacent applications and electrominerals (+11.1% in FY25), but these remain a minority of consolidated revenue and have not yet driven demonstrated multi-year outgrowth of the sector at the consolidated level.

bridge_assumptions.margin_delta_mechanism_note: Consolidated EBITDA margin (~15-16% in FY25-26 per company disclosures) is depressed by overseas-subsidiary drag: OFAC's Jan-2025 SDN-list designation of Russian subsidiary Volzhsky Abrasive Works (cash-repatriation restrictions, ~30% volume decline in affected quarters, ~Rs104cr exceptional charge) plus the voluntary wind-down of the loss-making German (CUMI AWUKO) and South African (Foskor Zirconia) units. As these are resolved/exited, consolidated margin should converge toward the already-demonstrated FY26 standalone EBITDA margin of 21.5% -- evidenced by the standalone/consolidated margin gap disclosed in FY26 results, not by an unevidenced aspirational assumption.

variant_perception.market_belief: The market is pricing CARBORUNIV off headline consolidated numbers -- revenue growth decelerating and consolidated PAT down sharply (Rs476cr FY24 -> Rs293cr FY25 -> Rs195cr FY26, a ~59% two-year decline) -- as a structurally weakening, low-ROE (~6.9%) industrial cyclical trading at a rich premium (PE ~58-82x across 2026 vs a peer average of ~42.6x).
variant_perception.whats_wrong_with_belief: A material share of the consolidated PAT collapse is attributable to identifiable, dated overseas one-offs rather than core-franchise deterioration: the Jan-2025 OFAC SDN designation of Russian subsidiary Volzhsky Abrasive Works (blocking USD/EUR payments and deposit withdrawals, ~30% volume decline in hit quarters) and the voluntary closure of loss-making German and South African units. Standalone (largely domestic) PAT actually grew ~29% YoY to Rs416cr in FY26 with EBITDA margin recovering to 21.5%, and all three domestic segments (abrasives, ceramics, electrominerals) grew mid-to-high single digits in FY25. The core India franchise is not the thing that broke.
variant_perception.persistence_mechanism: Headline optical ugliness -- consolidated GAAP PAT bundles a geopolitically-forced, largely non-recurring overseas write-off into the same line as a healthy domestic compounding business, and thin sell-side coverage for a ~Rs21,700cr smallcap industrial name means the market extrapolates the consolidated decline rather than looking through to the standalone trend.
variant_perception.gap_closing_event: Full resolution or completed exit of the Russia (VAW sanctions) exposure and the German/South African wind-downs, after which consolidated PAT should re-converge toward the standalone run-rate (~Rs400cr+) over the next several quarters -- an observable, dated set of disclosures rather than a speculative re-rating trigger.
